transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Recording id: ff-20270504-auroraish-01

Summary: Discovery focused on getting Auroraish to a prototype quickly; they are evaluating Hosted API for speed vs Private (VPC) for stricter telemetry controls. Notes and next steps captured.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, account exec on the Redwood Inference team. With me is Ravi, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Sofia (CTO): Good morning, thanks. Sofia here. We've got a pretty tight timeline—want to get something running for a demo to investors in six weeks.
[00:17] Ethan (Lead ML): Hey, Ethan. We're mainly evaluating time-to-first-token, cost for scaled inference, and some security constraints.
[00:25] Priya (Security): Hi, Priya. I'll focus on security and compliance questions. We handle telemetry that is quasi-PHI and need to understand audit logs and KMS requirements.
[00:34] Maya (AE): Great. Quick agenda: quick intro, how you want to use the API, walk through Quickstart credits and expected TFRT (time-to-first-token), then hosted vs dedicated/private tradeoffs, and next steps. Does that work?
[00:43] Sofia (CTO): Sounds good.
[00:46] Maya (AE): Ravi, do you want to kick off with the Quickstart flow?
[00:50] Ravi (SE): Sure. For most teams we see: sign-up, get onboarding credits, connect a small prompt set, run a couple of calls and streaming responses. With our PLG flow you can be sending your first token within hours; typical ramp to a working prototype is 24–72 hours depending on data prep.
[01:12] Ethan (Lead ML): When you say "credits", what's the usual amount? And do they expire quickly?
[01:18] Maya (AE): We typically provision $1–5k in credits for FastStart. I'll provision $3k for you which is intended to cover the initial bench and integration. They usually expire in 90 days but we can discuss extensions.
[01:30] Sofia (CTO): Good. The timeline is tight so the 24–72 hour is attractive. But our security team will probably push toward Private/VPC for telemetry retention.
[01:40] Priya (Security): Correct. Two quick asks: we need SOC2 report and a document that explains KMS/HSM options for key ownership. Also SAML/SSO for user access and RBAC.
[01:52] Ravi (SE): Understood. For Private (VPC) deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane option—that gives you the ability to keep keys in your KMS and restrict egress. For hosted customers we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys and detailed audit logs. I'll send the security pack.
[02:10] Markus (Product): Quick question — performance wise, if we go hosted what's the latency bucket for a 2k token request on a medium-size open model?
[02:18] Ravi (SE): For our curated open models, with our default runtime we typically see p50 latency in the 120–250ms per-token range depending on batching. For a 2k token request end-to-end you'll see a streaming response that depends on tokens per second; end-to-end for generation will depend on model choice and temperature but hosted will generally be faster to get started. If you need lower tails we recommend dedicated pools with pinned instances.
[02:46] Ethan (Lead ML): How about cost comparisons? Hosted vs private? If we self-host on-prem we can control hardware costs but lose the orchestration.
[02:55] Maya (AE): Hosted is usage-based — per-token + per-inference charges, and you get the runtime optimizations and scaling out of the box. Private has a platform fee + infra; Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with predictable monthly cost. We can provide a model-level unit economics sheet once we know your expected RPS and sequence lengths.
[03:14] Priya (Security): From compliance point, is audit logging tamper-evident? And retention periods configurable?
[03:21] Ravi (SE): Logs are stored with immutable entries and we surface them in the Console with retention options. For Private we can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging. For hosted, we support long-term export. We also support customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption if you need key separation.
[03:38] Sofia (CTO): Good. On the pilot, we'd like to define success as: 1) run our prompt suite with latency under X and 2) cost per 1k tokens under Y and 3) no PII leakage in outputs. Does Redwood do evaluation checks against prompt sets?
[03:53] Ravi (SE): Yes, we can run bench tests with your prompts; we'll set up a pre-flight where you upload a representative sample (anonymized). We can attach quality/regression metrics and compare models and quantization profiles. Also we can run a privacy analysis toolchain to flag likely leakage.
[04:10] Ethan (Lead ML): When you say "upload", does that go into your hosted environment? We prefer not to push raw logs.
[04:16] Ravi (SE): For hosted quickstart, samples are accepted over encrypted transit and you can request deletion after benchmarking. For stricter cases we recommend the Private VPC where the data never leaves your network.
[04:29] Maya (AE): To keep the prototype moving, a common path is: use hosted Quickstart credits to validate latency/cost and model fit, then if security gating fails, pivot to a Private pilot for production. That approach reduces time-to-first-token while still satisfying security.
[04:44] Priya (Security): What's the operational overhead to move from hosted to private? Do you need model re-quantization or changes?
[04:52] Ravi (SE): The runtime is the same across environments — we aim for parity. There may be kernel selection tweaks or quantization profiles optimized for on-prem hardware, but our onboarding SE will handle the migration. We also support model pinning so your rollout is predictable.
[05:07] Sofia (CTO): For the investor demo we'll likely do hosted unless security pushes back. So can you guarantee a TFRT of under 48 hours to a working demo?
[05:15] Maya (AE): Yes—if you share the prompt set and a short integration plan, we can have a direct call with your engineer, provision credits, and get a dev key within hours. Realistically a working demo within 24–48 hours is standard.
[05:27] Markus (Product): Are there any gotchas for streaming outputs and function-calling? We rely on structured JSON from model outputs.
[05:33] Ravi (SE): We support streaming and structured output enforcement. We have optional output validators and schema enforcement. We'll show examples on the SE deep dive.
[05:42] Ethan (Lead ML): For benchmarks, do you support continuous batching and KV-cache behavior to replicate production throughput?
[05:48] Ravi (SE): Yes — our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache. For bench runs we can emulate your expected concurrency and sequence length distribution to produce realistic unit cost and latency numbers.
[05:58] Priya (Security): On the SSO side — we need SAML and SCIM provisioning. Is that available in the hosted plan?
[06:03] Maya (AE): Yes, SAML + SCIM are supported on both Hosted with enterprise SSO and Private. We'll include SSO setup docs.
[06:10] Sofia (CTO): Ok, let's talk timeline and owners. We'll share a small anonymized prompt set by Monday. Can you provision credits and send the Quickstart guide?
[06:18] Maya (AE): Absolutely. I'll provision $3k in credits today and share the Quickstart link and the security pack (SOC2, KMS options, SAML details).
[06:26] Ravi (SE): I'll schedule a 1-hour SE benchmark session next week—I'll send a calendar invite with preflight instructions.
[06:33] Sofia (CTO): Great. One last question — pricing visibility: do you provide token-level cost breakdown in the Console?
[06:39] Maya (AE): Yes, Console has token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and we can attach tags for environment and model. We'll include a sample cost sheet.
[06:47] Ethan (Lead ML): Also curious about restart behavior—if the model variant falls back due to capacity constraints, can we control fallback policies?
[06:53] Ravi (SE): Yes—smart routing policies let you choose fallback variants, regions, or capacity tiers. You can also opt into automatic fallback to quantized variants to preserve availability.
[07:05] Markus (Product): For pilot success criteria—can you draft a short SOW template we can sign to lock the pilot dates?
[07:11] Maya (AE): Yes, I'll attach a short SOW/pilot template with success criteria and acceptance tests.
[07:17] Priya (Security): Please also include a checklist for audit evidence we'll need during the pilot.
[07:22] Ravi (SE): We'll include log export examples and how to set up SIEM ingestion.
[07:27] Maya (AE): Summing up: Maya will provision credits and send Quickstart + security docs; Ravi to schedule bench run; Auroraish to provide anonymized prompt set and target metrics. We'll aim to get a hosted prototype in 24–48 hours and then evaluate Private if required.
[07:43] Sofia (CTO): That sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone.
[07:46] Maya (AE): Thanks — we'll follow up by email with the attachments and invites.
[07:50] Ethan (Lead ML): Thanks, talk soon.

(End of recording)

References to shared artifacts: Quickstart guide: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart (sent). Security whitepaper / SOC2: https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper (to be sent). SE bench preflight checklist: internal link (invitation).
notes: Customer is PLG-forward but security-sensitive; recommended pattern: hosted Quickstart -> bench -> private pilot if gating. SE deep dive needed for benchmark; provisioned credits will be used to validate latency and cost targets.
